Title: Advice for turning my atomic notes into actionable insights and projects - Tips & Workflows - Supernotes Community
# Advice for turning my atomic notes into actionable insights and projects. I discovered supernotes a few weeks ago after going through a variety of different markdown editors (bear notes, obsidian, etc.). I fell in love with supernotes intuitive notetaking experience. Currently, my main purpose for using supernotes it to note down ideas and questions and try to build out my thought process around them. Eventually, the goal is to turn these atomic thoughts into blog posts and research essays. However, as I accumulate more notes, I am finding it difficult to turn these thoughts into actionable projects and insights. **QUESTION:** Does anyone have any advice on how I can begin forming my own process. I am aware of frameworks such as PARA and ACE, however, I think they restrict the capabilities of supernotes. More so posting this for the purpose of learning all the unique ways in people are using supernotes. Looking forward to hearing what people have to say! Powered by Discourse, best viewed with JavaScript enabled.

results.content:
Title: GitHub - thought-machine/please: High-performance extensible build system for reproducible multi-language builds. · GitHub
| Latest commit   History4,480 Commits 4,480 Commits |. Please is a cross-language build system with an emphasis on high performance, extensibility and reproducibility. It supports a number of popular languages and can automate nearly any aspect of your build process. See please.build for more information. Combine these two concepts with shared remote caches, and it makes for a blazing fast build system for any language or technology. Building software often involves more than just compiling code. Please does this through a consistent and seamless command line interface; there's no need to learn new build systems and technologies for different languages. The Docker & Kubernetes codelab covers building a Kubernetes based application with Please, including reliably deploying code to a local cluster, and pushing it to a remote registry. The Please build language is a full programming language. There are a high level set of build rules that make up a declarative DSL to define build targets, however you can drop into an imperative language that resembles python when necessary:. Additionally, `make` builds are not hermetic. Please builds only have access to files and environment variables they have explicitly been given access to. You can play around in the environment targets are built in with `plz build //some/target --shell`. Combine this with hermetic builds, and Please caching is never incorrect. The built-in languages are all defined in the same build language as you use to define your targets, demonstrating that there's nothing special about them. You have all the same tools Please has to expand your build definitions to satisfy your needs. # Building Please. To build Please yourself, run `./bootstrap.sh` in the repo root. If you'd rather not worry about installing the dependencies, we provide a prebuilt Docker image based on Ubuntu which is capable of building the whole thing for you: `docker run -it thoughtmachine/please_ubuntu`. Please is released & we consider it stable; we follow semver for releases, so major versions indicate potentially breaking changes to the BUILD language, command line or other behaviour.
